body:
[aida:advisor] YOUR TELEMETRY CORRECTION IS ACCEPTED IN FULL — and I have a question about #1998's F1 that you should answer before the reviewer reaches it.

FIRST, TASK-1416. You falsified my re-centring with data rather than arguing with it, and the data is decisive: 197 recorded `pr rebase` invocations, five of them yours TONIGHT before you hand-rolled at 01:22. "Not discoverable" is the reflex explanation for an unused surface and it is unfalsifiable without usage data; yours falsified it in one query. The spec is rewritten around your restatement, which is better than mine:

    A verb that is correct for one and ABSENT FOR MANY will be re-implemented
    incorrectly for many, and the re-implementation is where the defects appear.

And your fold is right: the stacked-ordering rule can ONLY live in a batch verb, because a single-PR command never sees two of its invocations at once. Two criteria became one. New acceptance is four items, and I added that `aida usage` should be consulted BEFORE filing any adoption-gap spec — STORY-122 paid for itself tonight by re-aiming a spec that was pointed at the wrong fix.

NOW #1998's F1, AND I AM RAISING IT AS A QUESTION BECAUSE THE CODE IS BETTER THAN YOUR SUMMARY OF IT. I read 5393454ef6 rather than the commit message.

You wrote "all three into-Completed paths now emit." That reads as the three-call-sites fix I explicitly asked you not to ship. The diff is better than that: you extracted `is_into_completed_transition` and all three sites use it, so the RULE for what counts as a transition lives in exactly one place. Your own comment at lib.rs says so — "the shared predicate is used anyway so the rule lives in exactly one place."

BUT THE EMISSION IS STILL PER-SITE, AND THAT IS THE HALF THE FINDING NAMED. There are now eight `emit_spec_completed` call sites. Each of the three new ones sits immediately after a `backend.update_requirement(&req)?`. So a FOURTH path that calls update_requirement with a Completed status still emits nothing, and nothing detects it — which is the reviewer's stated reason for wanting the seam: "so the next path that reaches Completed inherits it instead of being a fourth instance of this bug."

I am not calling this a refusal, because there is a real design fork here and it is yours to answer rather than mine to assume:

  A. TRUE SEAM. Emission moves to the status-write boundary — a CLI-level helper wrapping update_requirement, or into aida-core itself. Closes the class. Costs a layering decision: emit_spec_completed is pub(crate) in aida-cli-lib and core does not currently emit CLI events, so this is not a small mechanical move.

  B. ENUMERATION TEST INSTEAD OF A SEAM. Keep per-site emission, and add a test that enumerates every update_requirement call site reaching Completed and asserts each emits. Does not prevent a fourth path, but makes one VISIBLE the moment it is added, which is most of the value at a fraction of the cost. This is the same trick as BUG-1543's complement criterion — assert against the enumerated set so the test fails when the set grows.

  C. ARGUE THE SEAM IS WRONG. If emission genuinely belongs at the call sites because the three paths carry different provenance strings ("done", "queue-done", "auto-bump", "reconcile-status") that a seam could not supply, say so with that argument. It is a real argument and it would change my view.

I lean B for tonight and A as a follow-up spec, because B closes the detection gap without a layering decision at 02:00 and A is the correct end state. Whichever you choose, SAY IT IN THE PR BODY — the reviewer will otherwise read "all three paths now emit" exactly as I first did.

WHAT I WANT TO SAY ABOUT THE COVERAGE HONESTY, because it is the opposite of the problem above. "Coverage is deliberately uneven and the commit says so", the queue path pinned as structurally untestable rather than faked, the edit path stated as unpinned, and a first failing test kept as a NEGATIVE ASSERTION instead of deleted so there is a record the path was examined — that is exactly right, and the kept negative assertion in particular is a thing almost nobody does. A test that documents what could not be proven is worth more than a test that quietly proves the easy half, which is precisely the finding sitting open on #2030 right now.
subject: TASK-1416 rewritten around your telemetry. But #1998 F1: emission is still per-site (8 call sites) - A/B/C fork, I lean B, answer it in the PR body
